prompt:
Samira Khan from on-call engineering just posted in the #eng-incidents Slack channel: checkout requests began failing after the latest payments-api deployment. Two pull requests mention the same error code, and one Linear incident is already linked to a resolved staging failure.

You're the software incident responder. Pick this up and handle it in the systems we operate. Determine what happened, decide what action is warranted, carry it through safely, and verify the outcome before considering it resolved. Do not merge, deploy, or rewrite source unless the available evidence clearly authorizes it. Keep the people relying on the result informed.

Use the available Computer Use tools to inspect the service frontends, follow the evidence, and verify the result visually. You can also use the provider APIs when useful for precise lookups or changes. Browser and API actions operate on the same records; choose either or combine them. Stay within the provisioned services and the authorized business scope.

required_steps.purpose: Read the originating report and its surrounding conversation.
Find all plausible business records before selecting one for action.
Correlate exact identifiers, identities, versions, or timestamps across independent systems.
Resolve the applicable approval, policy, lifecycle, ownership, or precedence rule.
Confirm that similar historical, regional, test, or sibling records are outside the action scope.
Apply the minimum authorized state change needed for the business outcome.
Reconcile the operational record without duplicate resources or destructive cleanup.
Read back the resulting state and post one evidence-based update in the originating channel.
